subject: Kickoff: muNet multitask evolution
body:
Hi Jelena,

Kicking off the muNet project (Mar 2 – May 11). The research line from our open-source release: muNet evolves a pretrained network into a scalable auto-tuning multitask system, and the follow-up mu2Net adds dynamic introduction of new tasks into a large-scale multitask system without retraining from scratch. The released notebooks reproduce all published experiments, so reproduction cost is low.

Why product cares: the retrieval org currently maintains 11 per-task fine-tuning forks of the same base model. Every fork is its own eval surface, serving artifact, and on-call burden. One evolving multitask system that absorbs a new task on demand collapses that mess.

Milestones: end of March — muNet reproduction from the notebooks, ported to our training stack; mid-April — mu2Net-style dynamic task addition demonstrated on 3 internal retrieval tasks; early May — cost/quality comparison vs the fork farm and a Q3 adoption proposal.

Staffing and dependencies by Mar 13?

Anders
